subject: Hegner Center Property Reversion to City
overview: The Council celebrated the return of the Hegner Center to city ownership following council opposition to a private sale and addressed resident concerns regarding increasing aircraft noise and speeding on South Street.

items.title: Condolences and Tributes
items.summary: The council sent condolences to the family of Leona Greenwood, a long-serving Medford traffic supervisor.

items.title: Withdrawal of Item 16-741
items.summary: Item 16-741 was withdrawn by the petitioner.

items.title: Update on Increasing Aircraft Noise
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting an update from the administration and the city's Massport representative on aircraft noise, amended to request an emergency meeting with the mayor.

items.title: Traffic Calming and Truck Ban on South Street
items.summary: Approved a request for speed humps and a heavy truck ban on South Street to address speeding concerns, further requesting a Committee of the Whole meeting with the police chief and mayor regarding city-wide enforcement.

items.title: Return of Hegner Center to City Ownership
items.summary: The council discussed the successful reversion of 15 Maple Park Avenue to city ownership for one dollar, noting that council intervention blocked a previous attempt to sell the property for $650,000.

items.title: Utility Excavation and Restoration Update
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting an update on utility-related roadway excavation, restoration standards, and tree pruning responsibilities.

items.title: Routine Business and Meeting Recognitions
items.summary: The council requested crosswalk painting in West Medford Square, acknowledged early voting turnout, and recognized several local community festivals and networking events.
